policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'her little ones' does not distinguish the qere and ketiv forms; no mapped textual note decides the reading, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV explicitly renders the place-name as 'Luhith,' matching the qere reading rather than the ketiv.
ASV explicitly renders the name as 'Chemosh,' matching the qere reading rather than the ketiv.
ASV 'together' is compatible with both the qere and ketiv readings and no mapped textual note distinguishes them; the base fallback is retained.
ASV 'and sit' explicitly represents the qere imperative; the note 'art seated' is classed alternative_rendering and does not decide a textual reading.

ASV imperative 'wail' does not express the singular-versus-plural distinction between the readings; the alternative_rendering note concerns English wording and does not decide this unit, so the base fallback is retained.

ASV imperative 'cry' does not express the singular-versus-plural distinction between the readings; the alternative_rendering note concerns English wording and does not decide this unit, so the base fallback is retained.
ASV explicitly renders the place-name as 'Mephaath,' matching the qere reading rather than the ketiv.
ASV 'was he found' explicitly uses masculine agreement for Israel, matching the masculine qere rather than the feminine ketiv.
ASV 'He that fleeth' represents the qere's fleeing subject, distinguishing it from the ketiv causative form.
